title: Cyclone Akvan now forecast to hit Andhra as a severe, not very severe, storm on Friday
dek: The IMD's 9.30 am bulletin lowers the expected landfall winds to 100-110 kmph and keeps the crossing between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on Friday; extremely heavy rain is still forecast for coastal Andhra and now south Odisha.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclone Akvan strengthened into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal early on Wednesday, but the India Meteorological Department (IMD) no longer expects it to become a very severe storm. In its 9.30 am bulletin, the IMD said the storm is now likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on Friday, 20 November, as a severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph, down from the 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph it had forecast since Tuesday.

The landfall window and timing are unchanged, and the warnings for the coast remain serious. The IMD still expects extremely heavy rain of 21 cm or more at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh on 19 and 20 November, and has now extended that warning to south Odisha, with heavy to very heavy rain over north Odisha on both days. It kept its storm-surge forecast of 0.4-1.2 metres above the astronomical tide in seven Andhra Pradesh districts, and its forecast of heavy rain at isolated places in Gangetic West Bengal on Thursday and Friday.

## Latest bulletin

At 5.30 am IST on Wednesday the storm lay near 12.7°N, 85.5°E, about 580 km east of Chennai, 610 km south-east of Machilipatnam, 610 km south-south-east of Visakhapatnam and 730 km south of Gopalpur, having moved very slowly north-north-west at 3 kmph over the previous six hours, the IMD said in National Bulletin No. 21, which carries an orange-coded cyclone alert for Andhra Pradesh and the adjoining south Odisha coast.

Its forecast table shows sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph on Wednesday morning, rising only slowly to 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph by Thursday morning and holding at that strength until landfall. The storm is then forecast to weaken to a cyclonic storm by Friday evening, a depression by Saturday morning and a well-marked low-pressure area by Saturday evening as it moves north over Telangana and Chhattisgarh. In its 2.30 am bulletin the IMD had still forecast very severe strength from Thursday evening.

The highest storm surge is expected over Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari and Kakinada districts from Friday morning to the afternoon, with a surge of about 0.3 metres likely along those districts from the early hours to the evening of 20 November. Gale winds of 60-70 kmph gusting to 80 kmph are expected along the Andhra Pradesh coast from Wednesday evening, rising to 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph from Thursday night until landfall. Along the Odisha coast squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph are expected from Wednesday night, strengthening to 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph on Thursday and Friday.

The IMD's 9.30 am bulletin still warns of "major damage" to thatched and kutcha houses, power and communication poles, and standing crops and plantations in coastal Andhra Pradesh, waves of 9-14 metres from Thursday becoming "phenomenal" above 14 metres from Thursday night until landfall, and disruption to rail, road and air traffic. It advised a total suspension of fishing and offshore operations and that people living in coastal huts be moved to safer places.

Authorities have moved more than 80,000 people as a precaution, one report said, and Odisha has identified 2,04,070 people, 1,21,597 of them in Ganjam district, for possible evacuation and banned fishing off its coast from Wednesday morning to Friday, according to reports; National Disaster Response Force teams are on standby. Odisha, where heavy to very heavy rain is forecast in southern districts from 19 to 21 November, has deployed 74 rescue teams, 60 from its own disaster response force and 14 from the NDRF, in Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri and Puri districts, and has begun moving people out of landslide-prone and low-lying areas, according to reports. Odisha's Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the government had made "full arrangements to secure lives and property", and the Ganjam district administration said 107 pregnant women had been moved to safety, reports said. IMD Director General Mrityunjay Mohapatra said Odisha was likely to get "heavy rainfall, but not extremely heavy rainfall", unlike during Cyclone Arnab, according to reports.

## Where rain is forecast

The rainfall warnings in the 9.30 am bulletin on Wednesday, by the IMD's dates:

- Coastal Andhra Pradesh: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November; heavy to very heavy rain at a few places with isolated extremely heavy falls (21 cm or more) on 19 and 20 November; heavy rain at isolated places in north coastal Andhra Pradesh on 21 November.
- Odisha: heavy rain at isolated places in south coastal Odisha on 18 November; heavy to very heavy rain at a few places with isolated extremely heavy falls over south Odisha, and heavy to very heavy rain over north Odisha, on 19 and 20 November; heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 21 November.
- Eastern Telangana: heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 20 and 21 November.
- Gangetic West Bengal: light to moderate rain at many places, with heavy rain at isolated places, on 19 and 20 November. The Regional Meteorological Centre in Kolkata expects heavy rain of 7-11 cm at one or two places in North and South 24 Parganas and East and West Midnapore on Thursday, and in South 24 Parganas, the two Midnapores, Jhargram and Bankura on Friday.
- Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand: heavy rain at isolated places on 20 and 21 November; east Vidarbha and east Madhya Pradesh on 21 November.

## Warnings for fishermen and preparations

Fishermen have been told not to go into the southwest Bay of Bengal until 20 November, the westcentral Bay until 21 November, the southeast and eastcentral Bay until 18 November, and the northwest Bay, the waters off Odisha and West Bengal, from 19 to 21 November, the IMD said, and to suspend fishing operations totally in those areas.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu held a review meeting at the Secretariat on Monday and directed officials to deploy National and State Disaster Response Force teams in advance, keep energy department staff ready to restore power, and divert floodwater into reservoirs, with round-the-clock monitoring from the state's real-time governance centre, according to reports. Odisha has alerted all 30 of its districts and opened round-the-clock control rooms, and district officials in southern Odisha have ordered the early evacuation of vulnerable people, reports said. In Tamil Nadu, the state's relief commissioner urged people to follow only official bulletins, after private forecasters circulated computer-model forecasts showing a landfall near Chennai; the IMD's track keeps the storm well off the Tamil Nadu coast.

## Background

Akvan is the third cyclone to threaten the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts since late October. Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast in late October, and its remnants caused floods and a landslide in southern Odisha that killed at least three people in Kandhamal district. Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November, damaging crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 districts of Andhra Pradesh, according to the state government, though no deaths were reported.

November is one of the most active months for cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, after the south-west monsoon withdraws. The names used in the north Indian Ocean are drawn in sequence from a list contributed by 13 countries in the region; Arnab was proposed by Bangladesh, Murasu by India and Akvan by Iran, according to the published list.

For Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, a third storm in a month would arrive on soil that is already wet and over kharif crops, including paddy, that are close to harvest. Exact effects will depend on where the storm crosses the coast. The IMD's earliest outlooks pointed further north, towards the stretch between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur; its bulletins since Monday have moved the expected crossing south, and on Tuesday evening it widened the window to run from Nellore to Visakhapatnam, which it kept on Wednesday, when it also lowered the expected strength at landfall.

## What happens next

The IMD has moved from a pre-cyclone watch to a cyclone alert, the second of its warning stages; if the storm follows the forecast track it is expected to issue a cyclone warning, and then a post-landfall outlook, for the stretch of coast where landfall is expected. The landfall point may still shift; weather models differ on the storm's later movement and strength, according to reports citing the IMD's outlook.

## Key numbers

- 610 km: distance from Visakhapatnam at 5.30 am IST on Wednesday
- 580 km: distance from Chennai
- Severe cyclonic storm: forecast strength at landfall, lowered from very severe
- Around noon, 20 November: forecast landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam
- 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph: forecast winds at landfall
- 0.4-1.2 metres: forecast storm surge in seven Andhra Pradesh districts
- 21 cm or more: extremely heavy rain forecast at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha on 19-20 November
